mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised copy of valid passport or national identity card of each individual shareholder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state passport/identity authority and notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization only for documents originating in non-Hague Convention countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or corporate registry authority in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization only for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (statutes) of each corporate shareholder, including current registered address and director register extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or authentic official extract from the home jurisdiction registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney or board resolution for the proposed Luxembourg SARL incorporating attorney, appointing a Luxembourg notary and defining incorporation scope
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or general meeting of each corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Rule 12-02. Screening must cover PEP status, OFAC and UN Consolidated Lists, EU restrictive measures, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance Financial Sanctions Committee list. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to PEPs, high-risk third-country residents, and any person connected with aviation-related sensitive jurisdictions. Transaction monitoring and trigger-based revalidation are required for the lifespan of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), eRCS online portal via www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings and the SARL corporate name must be entered in Latin script. French is the standard registry language; German and Luxembourgish are also permitted where the name has already been approved by the RCS. A foreign-language or non-Latin-script name must be transliterated into Latin characters and filed as the official denomination. The name must be distinctive, non-misleading, and not contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the desired name is rejected, the applicant must file a fresh reservation through the LBR/eRCS portal with a modified distinctive denomination. A formal appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within three months of the written RCS refusal. Name extension is obtained by filing a new reservation request before expiry; each extension carries a statutory LBR fee and a fresh priority date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a genuine and stable registered office in Luxembourg, capable of receiving legal process and holding corporate records. Pure virtual office addresses are not acceptable for a trading SARL. Registered agent or co-working domiciliation may be accepted only if the company actually exercises management and control from that address and the statutory books are physically accessible there.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high. For the Medium_Risk_Enhanced aviation spare-parts distribution sector, the CSSF, RCS, or trade inspectorate may conduct an unannounced physical inspection; estimated likelihood is approximately 25% within the first 12 months of operation if the company has not yet demonstrated employee substance or fully maintained corporate records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as consolidated and modernized by the Laws of 10 August 2016 and 19 August 2016; the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is governed by Articles 180-1 to 180-28 (Title concerning private limited companies); subsidiary regulatory basis: Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2011 implementing the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice; electronic filing portal accessible via www.lbr.lu and Guichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) including the articles of association (statuts), executed before a Luxembourg civil-law notary, followed by RCS registration form and mandatory publication in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued and paid-up share capital EUR 12,000; 100% of cash subscriptions must be fully paid before signature of the notarial deed, deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte de garantie / compte bloqué) opened at a Luxembourg credit institution in the name of the company in formation, and released only upon entry of the company in the RCS; contributions in kind exceeding EUR 12,000 require a valuation report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé); 100% foreign ownership is permitted and no local incorporation of shareholders is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the founding shareholders approve and adopt the articles of association executed before a Luxembourg notary; (2) that the share capital of EUR 12,000, fully paid in cash, be held in a blocked escrow account at [Bank] and released solely upon RCS registration; (3) that the registered office be fixed at [Address], Luxembourg; (4) that [Name] be appointed sole manager (gérant) with full authority to represent the Company within the corporate purpose; and (5) that the manager initiate all filings, including RCS registration completion, VAT and social security registration, business establishment permit, and municipal and environmental clearances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked escrow account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. Spuerkeess, BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg) acting under CSSF anti-money-laundering rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate KYC file to the selected bank together with the draft articles of association, identity documents of all shareholders and the intended manager, and a statement of the aviation parts wholesale purpose. Deposit EUR 12,000 into the blocked account opened in the name of 'SARL [Name] en formation' and obtain the bank's blocking confirmation letter (attestation de dépôt / fiche de blocage) expressly stating that the funds are released only upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Proof of residential / business address
Source-of-wealth declaration and bank reference
Completed bank KYC and PEP forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide certified copies, a notarized warranty on source of funds, and auditor-confirmed corporate charts; if the bank refuses without a formal decision, re-route the application to a second Luxembourg bank and obtain a refusal letter for the notary's file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the notary the draft statuts, the bank blocking certificate, identity documents, and the certificate of good repute of the manager. Attend the signing session in person or grant a power of attorney to the notary's office. The notary verifies the legal capacity, the full payment of capital, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, and the 100% foreign ownership clause, then signs the deed and collects the fixed registration duty (droit d'enregistrement) of EUR 75.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Bank blocking certificate for EUR 12,000
Passports / IDs of shareholders and manager
Extrait du casier judiciaire (criminal record extract) of the manager
Residential status declaration required by Article 180-2 of the 1915 Law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect (unlawful purpose clause, unpaid capital, missing consent), amend the draft and fully disburse the capital; re-schedule the notarial session within five business days; if the notary refuses attestation, instruct legal counsel and engage another notary of the same chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation deed with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - electronic filing through www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the deed electronically to the RCS together with the required registration forms containing the corporate data: entity name, registered office, corporate purpose, capital structure, manager details and any restrictions on authority. Pay the RCS inscription fee online. The RCS verifies the file, assigns the national business number (numéro d'enregistrement) and issues the RCS excerpt, which constitutes legal existence of the SARL from the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (original)
LBR registration form for legal persons
Bank blocking certificate
Criminal record extract of the manager
Residential status and address declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (référé), the notary corrects the deficient items within the prescribed period; a refusal may be appealed before the competent chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg through summary proceedings, with damages claimable against the State under Article 8 of the 1915 Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) as official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, LBR transfers the incorporation particulars to RESA for the mandatory publication of the deed and the appointment of the manager. The publication appears online in the RESA gazette and constitutes notice to third parties; simultaneously, the bank releases the blocked share capital to the company's operating account upon presentation of the RCS excerpt and RESA publication proof.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized deed of incorporation
List of officers and registered office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is omitted or erroneous, instruct the notary to file a rectification notice with the RCS for correction; third-party reliance is governed by Article 14 of the 1915 Law, and the company may not invoke its deed against third parties until publication is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for corporate tax, VAT and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, file the VAT registration form (formulaire 810) with the AEDT indicating the wholesale of certified aircraft parts under NACE 46.69 and VAT exemption for intra-Community supply, if applicable. Register the company and its first employees with the CCSS as an employer; the manager-gérant is classified as an assimilated employee and must be declared to the social security fund. The ACD issues the corporate income tax file reference.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt
Notarized deed of incorporation
Manager's identity document
NACE classification sheet for the activity
Lease agreement of the registered office and warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT challenges the effective place of establishment, submit the lease, utility bills, bank statements and staffing evidence to demonstrate Luxembourg substance; if CCSS disputes the manager's social status, file an explanatory declaration; administrative rectification requests may be filed with the competent administration within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain business establishment permit and physical site clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction de la réglementation (authorization desk via Guichet.lu); local commune (municipal administration) for classified establishment approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online application for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) for the activity of wholesale merchant of certified aircraft parts, accompanied by proof of the manager's professional qualification and good repute. Simultaneously file the classified establishment declaration (classe 2) with the commune for the warehouse and offices, obtain the fire safety certificate from the municipal fire commission, and secure the occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM). Operation may commence only after all permits are granted.
required_dossiers: Completed establishment permit application via Guichet.lu
Certificate of good repute (casier judiciaire) of the manager
Evidence of professional management capability (diploma or three years of management experience in the last ten years)
Lease or ownership deed for registered office and warehouse
Site plan, fire safety dossier and electrical compliance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of the Economy or the commune refuses or conditions the permit, lodge a recours gracieux with the Minister, followed by a recours hiérarchique; if still unsuccessful, bring an action before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification, with a possibility of suspensive relief for irreparable harm.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction de la réglementation (Ministry of the Economy, Regulatory Department) acting under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions; plus the municipal administration of the commune where the warehouse is located for classified establishments under the amended Law of 10 June 1999.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (autorisation d'établissement) for wholesale merchant of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus; municipal authorization for the classified warehouse (établissement classé de classe 2); supplementary registration as a parts dealer with the Direction de l'Aviation Civile (DAC) of Luxembourg under Regulation (EU) No 748/2012 Part 21.A.124 when handling airworthiness-controlled components accompanied by EASA Form 1 release certificates.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 (declaration / municipal authorization) for a non-major warehouse of metallic aircraft components without hazardous chemical processes; full EIA under the amended Law of 22 May 2008 is not triggered below the Annex I thresholds, but a registration file must be lodged with the commune and the Administration de l'Environnement prior to operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater only: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 November 2010 on discharges into public sewers (COD below 2,000 mg/l, no AOX or heavy metals, pH 6.5-9.5); stormwater from roof and parking surfaces must be retained and treated per municipal drainage permit; VOC emissions limited to incidental degreasing - solvent consumption above 5 t/yr triggers the EU Solvent Emissions Directive 1999/13/EC and the amended Law of 21 June 1976 on air pollution; waste oils, lithium-ion batteries and aircraft fluid residues are hazardous waste under the Law of 21 March 2012 and must be collected by a licensed waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate of the municipal fire commission supported by an inspection of the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS): evacuation routes, fire doors, extinguishers, hydrants, smoke detection and electrical installation certificate; structural stability certificate for racking and mezzanine installations issued by an approved engineer in accordance with the Eurocodes and seismic category; occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering CE-marked handling equipment, low-voltage compliance, emergency lighting, first-aid and defibrillator provision, and a preliminary safety-and-health coordination dossier for any fit-out works.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu. VAT and indirect tax: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED), portal: https://aed.public.lu. Unified e-administration gateway for company and tax filings: https://guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity: (i) file Form 640 (demande d'immatriculation a la TVA) with the AED before the first taxable supply; the AED issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LV + 8 digits) and, where goods move across EU borders, an EORI number. (ii) If the foreign entity establishes a fixed establishment or branch in Luxembourg, it must also register with the Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) via an approved notary; the Guichet unique automatically transmits registration data to the ACD, which allocates a corporate tax file number (matricule). (iii) A resident Luxembourg SARL obtains its corporate tax file number automatically upon RCS registration; VAT registration follows the same Form 640 procedure and must be activated before the first taxable transaction. (iv) Direct-tax registration of a non-resident entity is not required absent a permanent establishment; Luxembourg-source income is then covered by specific reporting or withholding mechanisms. Standard VAT application processing time: 5 to 15 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide check-the-box elections; ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply (Article 168ter et seq. of the Income Tax Law). Available statutory elections: (i) CIT fiscal unity (integration fiscale) for resident companies directly or indirectly owned at least 95%, effective for tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2025; (ii) VAT group election under Article 60 of the VAT law for closely linked resident entities (financial, economic and organizational links); (iii) IP box regime electing the 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income; (iv) participation exemption election, declared in the annual CIT return, for dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (at least 10% or €1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period, subject-to-tax requirement); (v) securitization company (SIC) and alternative investment fund special regimes requiring prior AED approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutee, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident and established suppliers: €35,000 annual turnover small-enterprise exemption. Non-established foreign suppliers: no turnover threshold, mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. EU distance sales into Luxembourg: €10,000 EU-wide distance-sales threshold administered under the VAT OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing is phased in under the national law implementing Directive 2014/55/EU: from 1 July 2026 for large taxpayers and from 1 January 2027 for all other established taxable persons. Invoices must be issued and received in the PEPPOL-structured format via certified PEPPOL access points. No real-time fiscal clearance, no prior authorization, no API digital stamping exists; the Luxembourg model is post-audit access by the AED. VAT invoices and supporting records must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies qualify for 0% VAT where (i) goods are physically exported outside the EU, departing the customs territory of the Union within 90 days of dispatch, evidenced by an EU export declaration; or (ii) under Article 148(f) of Directive 2006/112/EC transposed in Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT law, spare parts, rotables and avionics supplied for the provisioning and maintenance of civil aircraft operated by airlines on international routes are exempt with credit, even where delivery occurs in Luxembourg, provided the airline operates international routes and the parts are destined for such aircraft. The supplier must retain a statement or certificate from the airline confirming international-route operations and the aircraft-specific purpose of the goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: EU single administrative document (export declaration) with movement reference number (MRN) registered in the Luxembourg customs DU/ECS system
Air Waybill or Bill of Lading or CMR evidencing physical dispatch from the EU to a third-country destination
Commercial export invoice and packing list
Proof of payment: SWIFT wire or inward remittance certificate evidencing receipt of consideration
For aviation surplus: EASA Form 1 release certificate, aircraft traceability records, and, where required, end-user/end-use declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No statutory FX repatriation deadline exists under Luxembourg law; the 180-day benchmark reflects trade-finance and escrow practice in the aviation spares model. If the AED determines that zero-rating was applied without sufficient documentary proof, it reassesses the supply at 17% VAT plus default interest of 0.8% per commenced month. In case of negligence or bad faith, proportional fines of up to 100% of the evaded VAT may be imposed; fraudulent conduct triggers criminal sanctions (fine up to €25,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years) and joint and several personal liability of the managing director. The AED may reassess within the normal 5-year period running from 1 January following the chargeable event, extended to 10 years in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the supervisory authority for banks and non-bank payment institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member state subject to the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and payments. There is no domestic exchange control regime, and the Euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Dividend distributions, shareholder loan repayments, and profit remittances are not subject to exchange control approval or obligatory conversion. The only legal constraints arise from general EU anti-money laundering, sanctions, tax transparency, and documentation requirements enforced via regulated banks and notaries. In practice, cross-border inbound funds and outbound commercial payments require a stated economic purpose, proper transaction references (e.g. purpose codes, invoice/contract references), and compliance with the CSSF AML/CFT circulars (notably CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the eurosystem impose no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or forced conversion of export proceeds. Export receipts may be held in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency in a Luxembourg bank account. Banks apply standard EU transaction reporting thresholds and wire-tagging requirements under the Wire Transfer Regulation (EU) 2015/847, but there is no statutory deadline for collecting or converting trade receivables. For operational treasury control, payment terms should nonetheless align with commercial contracts and typical open-account credit limits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR) and ancillary Escrow Account for aviation trade transactions
Operational Account and dedicated Escrow Account for high-value aircraft part disbursements
Operational Account (multi-currency) and Capital Escrow / blocked account for statutory capital contribution verification
Operational Account (EUR/USD) with transaction banking services for commercial LC and documentary collections
Operational Account and investment-grade clearing for corporate treasury services
Operational Account primarily for private client and asset-holding structures, less suitable for high-volume trading settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with legal limits. Luxembourg recognises e-money institutions (EMIs) under the Law of 10 August 2015 on payment services and e-money, and EU EMIs can operate in Luxembourg under the PSD2 EU passport. EMIs are viable only for ancillary low-value payables, supplier disbursements, and settlement rails where no credit or escrow perfection is required. EMIs are not permitted to take deposits or extend credit, and the safeguarding regime does not offer creditor protection equivalent to a licensed bank; therefore, an EMI is legally and operationally unsuitable as the primary escrow holder for the statutory minimum capital or for aviation transaction escrows. For high-value cross-border aircraft parts settlement, the counterparty bank must be a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution with direct SWIFT and TARGET2 access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally permit remote corporate account opening for non-resident directors after a completed video identification (DORA / GDPR-compliant), supported by a notarised board resolution and apostilled corporate documents. In practice, however, a physical or video-call interview with the designated authorised signatory and beneficial owner is always required to establish senior-management acceptance and mandate authenticity. A direct face-to-face interview with the bank's relationship manager, or at minimum a video conference with a notary/agent certifying identity, is required for structures using SARL holding companies with an ultimate owner not previously known to the bank. Banks may reject remote opening if the corporate registry search shows unexplained tax residency, or if the UBO's jurisdiction is a high-risk third country under FATF lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The corporate scope is distribution of surplus commercial aircraft parts, which may resemble dual-use or military-adjacent aviation hardware and trigger enhanced sanctions / export control screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregate dossier comprising (1) a signed end-use and non-military end-use certificate from the buyer and original equipment manufacturer certificates; (2) an ISIC 4659 / NAICS 423860 description clarifying excess, commercially decommissioned civil parts; (3) a copy of the operating licence issued by the Direction de l'aviation civile (DAC) or an aviation authority recognised by the EU; (4) a complete list of airworthiness certificates, EASA Form 1 / FAA 8130-3 documentation corresponding to each surplus rotable, if available; (5) the beneficial-owner declaration and recent RCS extract; (6) the board resolution approving the transaction; (7) trade control/dual-use licence, if any; (8) the purchase and onward-sale contracts evidencing margins and authenticity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value transaction with no physical receipt or invoice mismatch because parts move through multimodal non-named vessels/counters, resulting in hidden abandonment risk and customs declaration mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide transaction file containing (1) original commercial invoices with Incoterms matching freight documents; (2) customs import/export declarations or in-house customs broker confirmations; (3) a digital chain-of-custody ledger listing part serial numbers, photos or condition certificates, and logistic waybills; (4) a written confirmation from the clearing bank's trade finance desk that the load corresponds to the payment; (5) third-party independent inspection certificate for each lot above USD 250,000 in declared value.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden wire receipt from an unrelated jurisdiction or from a shell entity with opaque counterparty ownership intended as a capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the upstream shareholder relationship file: (1) the notarised corporate authorisation of the board of directors of the parent company; (2) the certified share register and UBO register extracts from the shareholder's home jurisdiction; (3) the bank confirmation of the originating institution; (4) a sworn declaration of source of funds; (5) the purpose code / intent of payment letter signed by the ultimate beneficial owner; (6) proof of actual subscription of SARL shares (RCS filing) and a receipt from the notary confirming that the subscribed capital is available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple small-dollar payments or frequent supplier advances to diverse jurisdictions without gross-margin consistency, resembling layering or third-party settlement risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The defence comprises: (1) the signed master trade agreement with each supplier; (2) a reconciliation of commercial invoices to part inventory management records; (3) a static treasury policy confirming single-bank concentration and no cash-outs through third-party accounts; (4) six months' projected cash flow and mid-month treasury forecast; (5) supplier onboarding forms with independent company verification, business registry extracts, and bank account beneficiary details matching the invoicing entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The minimum statutory capital of a Luxembourg SARL (currently EUR 12,000) is to be credited to a bank account opened in the LUX-SARL's name at a Luxembourg credit institution. The inward remittance from the parent or shareholder should be made via SWIFT MT103 using a transparent narrative such as 'SUBSCRIBED SHARE CAPITAL / INCREASE OF SHARE CAPITAL / SHAREHOLDER LOAN – SARL [NAME]'. There is no exchange-control approval, but banks apply standard verification under the Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT) and require the notarised articles of association, the RCS beneficial-owner extract, the shareholder resolution, and a board resolution of the Luxembourg SARL authorising the account opening. To prevent mis-mapping, the payment must include the exact corporate identifier (RCS/LU tax number) and bank reference. For foreign currency injections (USD, GBP, CHF), the amount is credited net of conversion spread; no central-bank licence is required. For capital increases exceeding substantial thresholds, a notary in Luxembourg may need to certify the capital subscription and payment; the contribution can be validated by a banker's certificate or a professional certificate of contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permissible clearing rails for outbound aviation spare-parts trade disbursements are (1) SWIFT MT103 for open-account and documentary collection settlement below EUR 500,000, using ICC Uniform Rules for Collections, and with the invoice and part numbers referenced in field 70; (2) irrevocable commercial letters of credit (LC) issued under UCP 600, typically confirmed by a bank in the supplier's country, for high-value rotables or when the supplier requires irrevocability; (3) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank covering transfers when an MT103 is not directly available; and (4) TARGET2 intra-SEPA transfers in EUR for EU suppliers and escrow release instructions to Luxembourg using domestic high-value payment clearing. Escrow Account release for aviation acquisitions must be authorised by a dual-control instruction comprised of the commercial confirmation issued by the SARL's compliance officer and the technical confirmation issued by the engineering or quality department.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forward contracts (spot + forward points) for trade receivable and payable currency matching
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) in currencies with limited onshore liquidity, taking care of Luxembourg and EU regulatory classification and clearing/trading obligation under EMIR
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/foreign-exchange) to manage long-dated aviation trade receivables or capital loan exposure
Vanilla FX call and put options to hedge large supplier contracts with uncertain invoice timing
Money-market deposits in foreign currency to reduce spread and preserve operational liquidity, subject to bank counterparty credit limit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of each financial year; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may face a court injunction and fines up to EUR 25,000; persistent default may lead to judicial or administrative removal from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner data in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year before 31 December; changes to UBO data must be filed within one month of the relevant event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Willful non-compliance may result in criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; administrative penalties apply for late or inaccurate confirmation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, normally due by 30 June of the following year unless an extension is granted by the tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to EUR 25,000, default interest of 0.5% per month on any unpaid tax, and reassessment risk for omitted municipal business or net wealth tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required if the SARL exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets over EUR 4,400,000, net turnover over EUR 8,800,000, or average workforce above 50 employees. An audit may also be required at the request of shareholders representing at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP) pursuant to the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts; EU-endorsed IFRS applies to consolidated accounts and certain supervised entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must verify and confirm, by 31 December each year, that all beneficial owner information recorded with the RBE is accurate and complete. Each equity transfer or UBO change must be reported to the RBE within one month and reconciled against the updated shareholder register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of shareholders' meetings and manager resolutions
Commercial and accounting books including journal, inventory, and supporting vouchers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate in Luxembourg City (17.00% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); aggregate rate varies by commune from 24.94% up to 28.69% at the maximum municipal rate of 10.50%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the SARL holds >=10% or the acquisition cost is >=EUR 1,200,000 and the holding period is >=12 months; IP box: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income under the OECD Nexus-compliant regime (effective rate approximately 4.98%); investment tax credit for eligible R&D tangible/intangible assets; notional interest deduction on new equity contributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (combined corporate income tax / municipal business tax return) filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu portal of the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD); tax advisors file via the secure ACD e-space with a signed power of attorney.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, irrespective of whether the SARL reports a profit or loss; the fiscal year is generally the calendar year but may follow the articles of association.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form 510 for a fiscal year ending 31 December must be filed by 31 December of the following calendar year (e.g. FY ended 31/12/2024 is due 31/12/2025); the competent bureau d'imposition may grant an extension upon written request. The tax assessment must be issued within 3 years of the end of the filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification block: legal name, RCS registration number, registered office address, taxpayer's national file number, and fiscal year opening/closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact RCS number (B-xxxxx) and state the accounting year-end; the SARL must disclose whether the central administration (siège de direction effective) is in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form and tax status: confirmation of the SARL election and the box 'résident' with full liability to corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick 'SARL' and 'résident'; if a non-resident gérant signs, attach an authenticated power of attorney accepted by the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder and ownership schedule: identities of partners, percentage holdings, changes of control during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose each non-resident shareholder's country of tax residence and, for treaty claims, their tax identification number and residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unadjusted net accounting result per the approved annual accounts (profit or loss before taxes, per Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS for consolidated reporting).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the figure to the audited financial statements of the Luxembourg branch of the spare-parts trading activity; include foreign-source gross income before treaty credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegrations (add-backs): non-deductible expenses, including fines, penalties, non-business entertainment, non-deductible value added tax, and excessive director fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support cross-border invoiced costs with service agreements and evidence of actual performance; undocumented charges to non-resident related parties must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ATAD interest limitation add-back: net interest expense exceeding 30% of EBITDA, subject to the EUR 3,000,000 de minimis threshold and the group ratio / equity escape clauses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare the EBITDA computation and, if the group ratio rule is invoked, attach the consolidated group statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustment: reintegration of hidden profit distributions or hidden capital contributions under Article 56 LIR where aviation spare parts are transacted with related parties otherwise than at arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the transfer pricing documentation (Master File / Local File) for the aircraft parts distribution function; the ACD requires a functional and risk analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible exempt income: dividends and capital gains under the participation exemption, and the IP regime deduction (80% of net qualifying IP income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For exempt dividends from foreign affiliates, attach proof of the >=10% holding or >=EUR 1,200,000 cost, the 12-month holding commitment, and the affiliate's tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis after offsetting loss carryforwards; computation of the aggregate charge at the CIT rate, solidarity surcharge, and communal corporate tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply losses in chronological order with evidence of prior assessments; losses older than 17 years (or older than 5 years if incurred before FY 2017) are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit under double tax treaties, the R&D and investment tax credits, and the notional interest deduction recapture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the foreign tax credit only on treaty-covered income; attach the relevant treaty article and foreign tax assessment; the credit is limited to the Luxembourg tax on the foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Affidavit and signature block: declarations of completeness, signature of the gérant, and reference of the certified tax advisor, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident gérant must digitally accept the declaration; false attestations trigger criminal and administrative sanctions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative penalty up to EUR 25,000 under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AOA), plus taxation d'office with an estimated assessment where the return is not filed; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) on the outstanding tax; willful non-filing or false filing constitutes tax fraud punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividend distributions; 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies (>=10% shareholding held at least 12 months) or where the Luxembourg participation exemption is met; applicable treaty rates (commonly 5% or 15%) may further reduce the withholding tax for non-EU residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Luxembourg paying SARL must submit Form 543 (exemption request for dividend withholding tax) to the competent bureau d'imposition before the distribution date, attaching: (i) the recipient's tax residence certificate (for a Luxembourg recipient, ACD Form 6; for a foreign recipient, a certificate from its tax authority, apostilled where required), (ii) an ownership chart evidencing the qualifying participation and the 12-month holding period, and (iii) the applicable treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive provision. The ACD issues a clearance/exemption prior to payment; if tax has been withheld, a refund claim must be filed within the treaty's limitation period, generally 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 0% on outbound interest and royalties; Luxembourg generally does not impose source withholding tax on interest or IP royalties paid to non-residents, and most tax treaties allocate exclusive taxing rights to the recipient's state of residence; exception: a 25% withholding tax applies to interest and royalty payments made to related parties resident in non-cooperative ('blacklisted') jurisdictions under the law of 19 December 2020, subject to grandfathering for agreements predating 1 March 2021.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File: mandatory for a Luxembourg entity forming part of a multinational group with consolidated net turnover above EUR 50,000,000 (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 December 2016); Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) is mandatory at consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more; the ACD may demand ad-hoc TP documentation below these thresholds for specific cross-border transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to UAE ESR; substance is enforced indirectly through Art. 159 LIR (effective management and control determines tax residence), the ATAD-1 general anti-abuse rule (Art. 6 AOA), CFC rules (Art. 164bis LIR), and the interest limitation rule. In practice, the ACD requires real presence (office, local staff, physical board meetings, commercial decision-making) before issuing a tax residence certificate or granting treaty/directive benefits. The EU ATAD-3 'Unshell' Directive, once transposed, will impose turnover-based fines and denial of tax residence certificates on shell entities lacking minimum substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting Form 510 with materially false or concealed income, fabricated invoices for aviation spare parts, or sham cross-border purchase/sale transactions; systematic under-declaration of gross margins in the aircraft rotables distribution business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under the Luxembourg General Tax Law: fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; reassessment of hidden profits with late payment interest at 0.6% per month and ancillary penalties (taxe proportionnelle) of up to 50%; publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who signs or directs a false filing is prosecuted as principal; the corporate veil does not shield deliberate fraud; civil joint liability under Art. 495 of the 1915 Company Law, restitution and confiscation orders, asset seizure, and preventive travel bans may be imposed by the investigating judge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Luxembourg SARL with no office, no local employees, board meetings held abroad, nominee gérants, and passive pass-through of funds from surplus aircraft parts trading; claiming Luxembourg residence solely to access tax treaty or EU Directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Refusal of the ACD to issue the tax residence certificate (Form 6); denial of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption and treaty relief; retroactive reassessment as a foreign tax resident; under the incoming ATAD-3 Unshell regime, fines of up to 5% of turnover for empty entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face personal liability for false attestations of residence and misrepresentations to the Luxembourg trade register; criminal exposure for aiding tax fraud; joint liability for uncollected taxes where the entity is treated as failing (comblement du passif); travel bans during money-laundering investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Aircraft parts purchased from or sold to non-resident related parties at non-arm's length prices; consistent book losses or routine margins without a functional analysis; undocumented management fees or brand royalties draining profit to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under Art. 56 LIR with recharacterization of hidden profit distributions; denial of deductions for undocumented cross-border charges; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; administrative fines; potential CFC attribution or exit tax where the foreign affiliate retains the profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve mispricing without an economic analysis may be held jointly liable for the company's tax arrears as faute de gestion under Art. 495; liability for unlawful distributions under Luxembourg company law; commercial court liquidation proceedings (action en comblement du passif) where the mispricing rendered the SARL insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Swift-wire or escrow payments for aircraft parts involving sanctioned air carriers, opaque beneficial owners, or circular transactions without commercial reality; failure to file a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF); supplying certified civilian aircraft rotables to embargoed destinations with dual-use exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) of up to EUR 5,000,000 for regulated professionals; criminal money-laundering penalties under Arts. 506-1 and 506-2 of the Criminal Code with imprisonment up to 10 years for natural persons and fines up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal entities; confiscation of inventory and freezing orders by the CRF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who omit UBO registrations, forge compliance documentation, or facilitate OFAC/EU-embargoed deals face criminal prosecution, preventive travel bans, confiscation of personal assets, and disqualification from holding directorships; operating unlicensed payment collection without a PISP/e-money authorization adds separate regulatory exposure.
